title: GPU ingress sentinel and gradual degradation runbook
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Summary:

This ticket implements an 'ingress sentinel' and a formal gradual-degradation runbook to prevent and mitigate hosted GPU capacity exhaustion events that create long queues, hardened throttling, and noisy scaling reactions. The goal is to reduce tail latency spikes and avoid hard evictions by detecting early queue resonance, applying smooth tenant pacing, and enabling non-disruptive fallbacks (quantized model variants / regional spillback).

Scope of work:
- Implement an 'ingress sentinel' service that aggregates per-pool signals (queue depth percentile, 95/99/99.9 tail latency, GPU util, recent eviction rate) and publishes a consolidated health score every 10s.
- Add a token-bucket based tenant pacing governor applied at admission time keyed by tenant and model variant; pacing is by token-cost-per-second (tokens = estimated tokens * weight).
- Create gradual-degradation policies: 1) reduce maximum tokens per request, 2) prefer quantized-compatible variants, 3) route to dedicated/burst pools if available, 4) controlled rejection with informative error codes for downstream clients.
- Runbook: define responder playbook for on-call and SRE to follow when sentinel health < threshold (actions, dashboards, paging steps, rollback guidance).
- Telemetry: add sentinel metrics, tenant pacing events, and degradation decisions to observability and billing dashboards for retro and billing reconciliation.

Rationale and chosen approach:
We observed multiple incidents where sudden workload patterns produced queue resonance: prefetching + heavy KV-cache misses produced long-lived requests that blocked GPU slots and triggered aggressive autoscaler step-ups and evaporation loops. Rather than aggressive immediate eviction (which worsens tail latency), ingress sentinel enables early, measured intervention. Token-bucket pacing smooths ingress over seconds and preserves QoS for steady producers. Quantized fallbacks reduce per-token compute cost without immediate autoscale churn.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not implement new autoscaler algorithms (that is a follow-up). It focuses on admission/routing and runbook automation only.
acceptance_criteria: Ingress sentinel exports a composite health score metric (sentinel.health.score) at 10s cadence for every GPU pool
Tenant pacing governor enforces per-tenant token throughput; tests show 90% reduction in queue growth for synthetic high-burst traffic
Two controlled degradation actions (quantized fallback and reduced max tokens) apply automatically under sentinel thresholds with audit logs
Runbook doc linked in Confluence and reviewed by SRE + Oncall, with clear paging and escalation steps
Dashboards surface sentinel signals, pacing events and correlating cost delta per tenant
comments: 2026-02-18 Sofia Martinez: Kickoff — documented symptoms from last outage (queue depth correlation with KV-cache churn). Agreed to prototype sentinel in a lightweight service to avoid runtime entanglement.

2026-02-22 Derrick Huang: Prototype submitted — sentinel can compute median-of-tail and exponential smoothing. Initial false positives on synthetic bursts; tuned smoothing window to 3x baseline request RTT.
2026-02-25 Priya Rao (SRE): Reviewed runbook draft. Requested explicit 'restore' path and a cooldown for automated actions (default 120s) to avoid flip-flopping.

2026-02-26 Derrick Huang: Tenant pacing implementation pushed to feature branch. It uses estimated_token_cost = prompt_len + completion_budget, multiplied by tenant_weight. Tests against replayed production traces show admission smoothing but increased 95 P99 billing metadata emissions.

2026-02-28 Mariana Ortiz (PM): Confirmed customer communication template for controlled rejections; added guidance for SDK retries with jitter and backoff. Also recommended adding a manifest for tenants that opt-in to prioritized prewarm.

2026-03-01 Derrick Huang: Merged runtime fallback logic (prefers quantized variant if available). Integration tests pass in canary with reduced cost per-token and 8% lower GPU utilization during high-burst scenario.
2026-03-02 Sofia Martinez: Roadmap sync — follow-ups logged (autoscaler integration, tenant opt-in UI, billing reconciliation). Scheduling runbook tabletop on 2026-03-10.
notes: Telemetry considerations: sentinel.health.score must be tagged by pool_id, region, and release. Store last 6 hours at 10s granularity for forensic replay.

Trade-offs: token-bucket pacing reduces elastic capacity needed but can increase client-visible latency for bursty tenants. We will introduce a tenant SLA flag to allow opt-outs with higher cost commitments.
Performance: pacing and sentinel are lightweight; added CPU usage estimate ~1 vCPU per 50 pools. Memory negligible. Avoid co-locating with model process to keep blast radius small.
Operational: add a 'soft-degrade' metric that counts how many requests were served by fallback quantized models to measure quality regression risk.
Follow-ups: ENG-271846 (autoscaler integration with sentinel signals), ENG-271847 (console UI for tenant pacing toggles), PM-40213 (customer opt-in workflow)

Risk: inaccurate estimated_token_cost for multimodal requests may under/over-throttle — we will add an online calibration job that compares pre-estimates with actual token consumption over a sliding window.
